text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Bank Austria's supervisory board has given its approval for management to put forward an offer for Creditanstalt. Chamber of Economy secretary Guenther Stummvoll, a conservative, is furious about the planned market concentration.
- Latest investigations show the most recent letterbombs were made 1995 in a kind of serial production.

- In mid-1997 Transport Minister Rudolf Scholten intends to present a new telecommunications law for the liberalsiation of the market in 1998. Energy suppliers and federal railways OeBB will receive special licences for data communications.
- Vienna's retailers expect turnover in sales ahead of Christams to be about two percent lower this year.
- Bank employees will get 1.9 percent higher wages from February 1, 1998.
- Bank Austria's 16-bilion-schilling bid for Creditanstalt could lead to a bitter row in Austria's government coalition, the newspaper says.
- Social Democrat chief whip Peter Kostelka wants to have a say in Austria's conservative dominated defence ministry.
- Austria's postal service monopoly plans to raise postage prices next year.
- The third mobile phone licence will be auctioned off in a tender starting March 1998, Transport Minister Scholten said.
- Conservatives say "no" to a merger of Creditanstalt and Bank Austria.
- Parliament will decide on longer shopping hours today.
- The conservative People's Party will not be able to stop a takeover of Creditanstalt by Bank Austria. The newspaper expects further concentrations in the market should the deal go ahead.
- Austrian Airlines, Lauda Air and Tyrolean Airways have told Vienna airport they will carry out their own ground work on planes if the airport does not lower fees by January.
